title: IP63104: Jurisprudence And Judicial Process
text:
Syllabus
Syllabus mentioned in ERP

Theories of Law, Schools of Jurisprudence- relevancy, limitations, contribution
to the development of law and legal institutions, Contemporary understanding of
positivism and natural law, Law as practice of the court, Jurimetrics, Law and
Science, Law and Society, Law as a synthesis of order and justice, law and the
enforcement of morals-Critical Legal Studies Movement, Critical Race Theory,
Feminist Legal Theory, Theory of Justice and Minimalist State. Judicial process
in pursuit of Constitutional goals and values- Law of Precedent-New dimensions
of judicial activism and structural challenges – Institutional liability of
Courts and judicial activism-Scope and limits, Reference:1.Julius Stone, The
Province and Function of Law, (2000), Universal New Delhi. 2.Cardozo, The
Nature of Judicial Process (1995), Universal, New Delhi3.Prof. Michael Freeman,
Lloyds Introduction to Jurisprudence, (2014), Sweet and Maxwell.4.Murphy Mark
C, An Essay on Divine Authority (Cornell Studies in the Philosophy of
Religion), (2002), Cornell University Press.5.A.Laxminath, Precedent in Indian
Law: Judicial Process, (2012) Eastern Book Company.
